Geographic focus:
Global (high northern latitudes: Canada, Russia, Alaska, Scandinavia); boreal forest belt

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — current observed shifts in Alaska/Canada referenced
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [NO]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — modelled projections across 21st–22nd centuries

Synopsis:
Climate-driven warming and increasing disturbance frequency (wildfires, storms) are accelerating a structural shift in boreal forests from evergreen-dominated (spruce, fir) to deciduous-dominated ecosystems. Deciduous trees recover faster post-disturbance and benefit more from longer growing seasons and higher soil nitrogen. This transition has measurable implications for global carbon sequestration, water and energy cycles. The shift is already empirically observable in North America.
